newsitem.title: POLAND: Weather, school-leavers push Polish jobless down.
newsitem.headline: Weather, school-leavers push Polish jobless down.

text.p: Good weather allowing for more seasonal jobs and fewer school-leavers registering as unemployed pushed Poland's unemployment down in October, deputy Labour Minister Maciej Manicki said on Thursday.

"Weather was favourable in October... and an increasing number of school-leavers take vocational trainings or take advantage of other programmes...rather than register themselves as unemployed," Manicki told a news conference.
The unemployment rate fell to 13.2 percent of the workforce last month from 13.5 percent in September and 14.7 percent in October 1995.
Manicki said unemployment was likely to slightly increase in the next few months because many seasonal jobs in the farm and construction sectors would end.
He said October's unemployment fell in 48 of Poland's 49 provinces and was below nine percent in several large urban regions, while above 25 percent in four northern provinces.
Nearly 60 percent of unemployed were women and 38 percent of the jobless had already lost a right to unemployment benefits.
